# Chapter 6: How computers execute instructions

<!-- BEGIN HEADER (generated by tools/build.py) -->
> [Home](../../../../README.md) › [Part I — Computer Science Foundations](../../index.md) › [1. Computer Fundamentals](../index.md) › Chapter 6: How computers execute instructions

- **Status:** Drafted · 7 syllabus topics
<!-- END HEADER -->

The previous chapter named the parts of a computer. This chapter shows them working together on a program, which is the idea that turns a pile of components into a machine that can run any software. It explains the one loop every processor repeats, **fetch, decode, execute**, and the two ways that loop meets the rest of the system: **interrupts**, which let hardware events break into a running program, and **system calls**, which let a program ask the operating system to do what it is not allowed to do itself.

The lessons build a small computer in Python, with an assembler and a simulator you can run, so that every idea in the chapter can be watched step by step. Lesson 1 builds a computer that follows instructions. Lesson 2 extends it with a timer, privileged instructions and a tiny kernel, and shows what goes wrong when an interrupt handler is careless.

This is the last chapter of Subject 1. Subject 3, *Digital Logic and Computer Organization*, returns to the processor in hardware detail, and Subject 4, *Operating Systems*, returns to interrupts and system calls from the operating system's side. Read the lessons in order.
